findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employee was observed donning gloves without handwashing. PIC was made aware. Ensure that employees are aware and remember to wash their hands before donning gloves in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Inspector observed a series of ready to eat food items such as salads, dressings, fruits, and other condiments not properly dated and marked as required in the second walk-in cooler at the deli department. Discussed with PIC and PIC instructed employees to immediately date mark the items on the shelves. Ensure that all food items such as the one mentioned are properly dated marked at all time for safety. 

(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed eggs being stored over mushrooms in the walk-in cooler in the meat department. PIC was made aware of the appropriate storage order for food items and the eggs were moved a shelf below the mushrooms in order to correct the storage order. Ensure that all food items are stored appropriately to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

Ensure that cold holdings are often checked to ensure they maintain the adequate temperature to avoid food spoilage.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text: 750.100 - Two cartons of moldy strawberries were observed in the walkin cooler. Both containers and cardboard flat were discarded. Check produce daily and discard questionable foods. Do not keep any portion of moldy produce for any reason. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750.140b - (R) Container of mostaccoli prepared earlier today did not have proper label - missing time stamp to properly monitor cooling process. Management was advised of proper cooling practices and labeling. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F/below.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.151 - Products in walkin cooler had date marks that indicated they were past the 7 day time frame for use and/or contained questionable dates. Cream of mushroom had prep date of 11/1, and fried chicken tenders had date of 10/31 on container. Also, a container of mac-n-cheese had a use by date of 11/9 but no prep date. All foods in question were discarded. Manager on duty stated the chicken tenders for sure had an old label on the container but still discarded the product at the inspector's request. Ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be properly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. **All staff needs to be trained on proper dating and use of foods.**

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Multiple foods in the hot case had internal temperatures of 115F-130F (livers, gizzards, mashed potatoes, gravy, green beans, & mac-n-cheese). Manager stated some products were just switched recently and new water was added to the wells below. Possibly having the doors open could have allowed some heat to escape the case. Questionable products were discarded. Freshly prepared foods had temperatures of 140F-150F. Maintain hot PHF at135F/above at all times. **Other foods were at 135F/above in the same holding case, and the heating element/water wells appeared to be holding temperature (146F-190F surface temperatures). Temperature settings for bottom heating element and heat lamps were adjusted to higher settings. Monitor hot holding temperatures in the case and - getting in and out of cases allows heat to escape and could be the reason why some foods were out of temperature**

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Mostaccoli had internal temperatures ranging from 55F to 73F. A time was not written on the label, but employee responsible for prep told manager it was made around 10:45am. Product was discarded during the inspection. Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in additional 4hrs (total cooling time 6hrs). Foods must be separated into smaller batches, placed on ice baths, and stirred frequently to allow for rapid cooling. Place cooling foods in clean storage areas separate from raw foods, and leave foods uncovered until cooling process is complete. **Note: heavy condensation on a container of chicken and noodles dated 11/8 indicated proper cooling may not have occurred with that product also, but the temperature was 30F at the time of the inspection** Properly cool cooked PHF.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750.820c - Container of fried chicken tenders had old sticker with a date of 10/31 on it. (product was discarded see #3a). All equipment and utensils must be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil. Remove old stickers to properly clean all surfaces of lids and containers. If items are still soiled after ware washing process is complete or sticker residue remains then repeat the process as many times as needed to allow for proper wash, rinse, sanitize of all surfaces of equipment and utensils.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils

Keep storage drawers and containers clean to protect utensils from potential contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)

Sinks shall be cleaned prior to use. **Educate employees in deli on proper setup/use of 3 part sink**

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
